correctness.rationale: An exact beta-moment expansion yields the differentiable angular pair kernel. Its quarter-turn/half-turn curvatures give positive explicit integrals. Fourier diagonalization of the four-cycle plus diagonals gives the stated Hessian spectrum. Reweighting as a probability measure shows the ratio u/v is the expectation of a strictly increasing rational function under a strictly decreasing likelihood-ratio family, so it crosses one exactly once. Exact rational enclosures of pi and log(2) certify opposing signs at exponents two and three. Taylor expansion supplies the sharp quadratic coefficient and beta moments prove the large-exponent condition-number asymptotic. The embedded checker independently verifies curvature and finite differences; finite tests are not treated as all-exponent proofs.
